title: Which apartments are over-priced? Ensembles, market segments and a neural network on krisha.kz ads
subtitle: Endterm: the Week 5–8 methods applied to our 4,815 Astana and Almaty listings, on the same saved test split as the Midterm
s2_title: Question, data and what changed since the Midterm
s2_question: Which apartments in Astana and Almaty are asked above or below what comparable apartments go for, and by how much?
s2_left: Same data:: 4,815 krisha.kz ads scraped 4–8 Oct 2026; target = asking price, KZT
Same split:: 963 test ads saved at the Midterm, read from the file, used once (Section 6)
Same metric:: MAE in KZT (the user's money) and MdAPE (registration goal: median error < 10 %)
Midterm result:: linear model on log price, test MAE 8.65 M, MdAPE 11.3 %, goal not reached (re-run with the Endterm feature list: 8.66 M, 11.27 %)
Users:: buyer flags an ad > 20 % above the estimate; seller gets a starting price; realtor a reference
s2_right: Fix 1 · question:: from “predict the price” to “which ads deviate from the market, by how much”
Fix 2 · data ethics:: free text checked for contact data: 0 phone numbers, 7 realtor handles masked
Fix 3 · features:: has_detail dropped (a scraper artefact); 10 ads with coordinates in the wrong city → missing
Fix 4 · model choice:: by 5-fold CV MAE only; the Midterm had picked by test MAE
Added:: forest, boosting, XGBoost, LightGBM, randomised search, blend, K-Means, DBSCAN, PCA, segment feature, PyTorch MLP
s3_title: Ensembles: the forest removes the tree's variance, boosting its bias
s3_bullets: Fully grown tree:: train MAE 0.00 → CV 11.25 ± 0.73 M: memorises, high variance
Random forest, 300 trees:: CV 8.00 ± 0.37 M, SD halved: averaging cancels the variance
Gradient boosting, 100 × depth 3:: CV 7.87 ± 0.33 M, smallest train→val gap (1.3 M): shallow trees, bias removed by summing
Histogram boosting (default):: CV 7.01 ± 0.38 M, 2.1 M below the linear model (9.10 ± 0.61) = 3–4 fold SDs
Learning rate × trees:: 0.3 flattens at 450 trees (6.99 M), 0.1 still improving at 600 (6.74 M), 0.03 underfits (7.44 M); differences ≈ one fold SD
s4_title: Tuning bought one fold SD for boosting and nothing for the forest; XGBoost and LightGBM confirm the score
s4_bullets: RandomizedSearchCV:: 25 forest + 40 boosting + 20 XGBoost + 20 LightGBM settings, same 5 folds, scored by MAE in KZT
Forest:: best 7.99 ± 0.38 M vs default 8.00: insensitive to its settings
Boosting:: best 6.62 ± 0.35 M vs default 7.01: lr 0.12, 7 leaves, 600 iterations, 5 rows/leaf; the five best within 0.11 M, all with many iterations and small leaves
XGBoost 6.64 ± 0.32, LightGBM 6.75 ± 0.28:: three libraries within a third of a fold SD; the 6.6 M floor belongs to the data, not the library
OOB check:: forest OOB MAE 7.66 M vs CV 7.99 M, the two estimates agree
Permutation importance:: shuffling area +17.5 M MAE, lon +7.2, lat +6.4, year +2.8, ceiling +2.1, district only +1.3: coordinates beat district names 5×
Blend forest + boosting:: 6.95 M, between its parents; extra trees 8.69 M: no help
s5_title: Market segments: K-Means within each city; DBSCAN finds one dense cloud per city plus 29 unusual ads
s5_bullets: Inputs:: log area, rooms, floor, floors in building, year, lat, lon; price never an input
k chosen per city:: silhouette + inertia + stability (ARI on 80 % subsamples ≥ 0.9, no cluster < 30 ads) → Astana 4 segments (silhouette 0.21, ARI 0.97), Almaty 5 (0.25, 0.97)

Segments in words:: Astana: mass market 45 m² new (912 ads), large family flats 92 m², tall-tower flats floor 13/18, old low-rise 2006 at 477 k/m² (cheapest). Almaty: premium high-rise 848 k/m², club-house flats 87 m², Soviet centre 1976 at 766 k/m², small new west, cheap north-east 632 k/m²
Silhouette 0.21–0.25:: cuts through a continuum, a description, not islands
DBSCAN, eps 1.40 at the knee, min_samples 14:: 2 clusters = the two cities, 29 noise ads (0.8 %)
Noise = real unusual objects:: 140 m² on floor 42/43, a 187 m² 6-room penthouse (listed twice), a 1-room flat on 11/34; kept, but used as a “few comparables” warning
s6_title: PCA describes the table but does not help the model; a segment feature adds nothing
s6_bullets: 10 numeric fields:: 5 components for 80 %, 7 for 90 % of the variance; the last one is 0 % (lat and lon anti-correlated across the two cities)
PC1 = new high-rise in Astana vs old low-rise in Almaty:: total floors 0.41, lat 0.40, year 0.34, lon −0.40
KNN on components:: 11.5 M (90 % var.) vs 11.1 M raw; Ridge 10.6 M vs 9.1 M raw: every reduction costs
Midterm KNN on size + location only (10.2 M) beats both:: columns chosen by meaning beat directions chosen by variance
Boosting + in-fold K-Means segment:: 6.65 ± 0.31 vs 6.62 ± 0.35 M: the model already carves those regions itself
s7_title: A PyTorch network ties the linear model and loses to boosting by six fold SDs
s7_bullets: Setup:: same encoded inputs (71 columns), standardised log price, L1 loss, Adam, dropout, weight decay, early stopping on 15 % of the fold, same 5 folds
No hidden layer = linear by gradient descent:: 9.26 ± 0.57 M vs 9.10 for the Midterm linear model, the loop is right
64 / 128-64 / 256-128-64 units:: 8.82 / 8.90 / 8.86 M, all within 0.1 M; scikit-learn MLP 8.86 M confirms
Curves:: training loss keeps falling, validation stops after 10–30 epochs and wanders: memorising; lr 0.05 makes it jump between 8.5 and 10.5 M
Verdict:: 2.2 M behind tuned boosting (6.62 M) on every fold; 3,852 tabular rows with threshold effects are tree territory, 0.3–0.7 s per fit on one CPU thread
s8_title: One table, chosen by CV, tested once: tuned boosting reaches MdAPE 9.1 %, the 10 % goal is met
s8_bullets: Chosen by CV MAE:: tuned histogram boosting, 6.62 ± 0.35 M
Test, used once:: MAE 6.29 M (bootstrap 5.56–7.14), MdAPE 9.13 % (8.31–9.88), R² 0.855
vs Midterm on the same 963 ads:: 8.66 M, 11.27 %, R² 0.712: error in money −27 %

LightGBM, XGBoost, blend and default boosting look as good on the test column (6.2–6.6 M):: we do not switch, that would be choosing on the test set; three libraries agreeing is what makes the number trustworthy
s9_title: Errors: the expensive bands improved most; what is left sits in the text
s9_bullets: By price band (MdAPE, Endterm vs Midterm):: 20–50 M 8 % vs 10 %; 80–150 M 12.9 % vs 21.9 %; > 150 M 16.6 % vs 31.8 %
Bias:: cheap ads over-estimated by 9 %, luxury under-estimated by 14 % (15 ads > 150 M)
Worst cases:: “cash only, assignment of rights” (13.9 M predicted 20.8), rough state, a 276 m² designer duplex at 525 M predicted 245: text-only reasons or no comparables
Midterm's worst 8:: 364 m² penthouse 133 % → 33 %, Nura flat 68 % → 3 %; four of eight stay above 40 %
Buyer's flag:: 93 of 963 ads (10 %) ask > 20 % above the estimate; owners and agents equally (10 %); 28 ads with no comparables get a warning (MdAPE 12.9 % vs 9.0 %)
s10_title: Conclusions, limitations and the plan for the Final
s10_left: Answer:: structured fields give a 9.1 % median error; one ad in ten asks > 20 % above comparable apartments, one in twenty > 20 % below
Ensembles:: −27 % error, mostly in the expensive bands; tuning worth one SD; XGBoost and LightGBM land at the same score; blend and extra trees no help
Unsupervised:: one dense cloud per city; segments describe, DBSCAN flags unusual ads; PCA shows 7 real dimensions, none of them price
Network:: ties linear, loses to boosting; not worth it on 3,852 tabular rows
Importance:: size and coordinates carry the model; what remains is not in the fields
s10_right: Limitations:: asking ≠ sale price; one October snapshot, one site; 15 luxury test ads; the test set is seen at every stage; tuning on the comparison folds
Final 1 · text:: TF-IDF of the sanitised description on cross-fitted residuals of the boosting model, judged on the worst cases
Final 2 · photos:: pretrained-CNN embeddings of up to 3 photos per ad as a second residual correction
Final 3 · app:: fields + text + photos → estimate, segment-based interval, over-pricing flag with the “few comparables” warning
Final 4 · honest check:: re-scrape in November as a temporal hold-out; the saved split stays unchanged
